statement: Sell-side price targets on NVIDIA were mostly raised in late August and early September 2026, consistent with analysts expecting data-center GPU revenue to keep growing, though the target range is unusually wide.
why: Clustered target increases are an indirect read on whether the sell side still expects NVIDIA's data-center revenue line to expand, which is the single largest merchant-GPU demand proxy.

impact.mechanism: Upward revisions to analyst valuations generally follow upward revisions to modeled data-center revenue, so the cluster of raises implies expectations of continued accelerator demand.

evidence.excerpt: Phillip Securities raised its price target 'from $285.00 to $300.00' and maintained a buy rating (research note issued Monday morning, early September 2026). Citigroup reaffirmed a buy rating and 'issued a $315.00 price objective (up from $300.00)' in a note dated Thursday, August 27.

reasoning: The document reports price-target changes and ratings, not revenue guidance. Inferring a demand signal from valuation targets is an interpretation, so this is recorded as a hypothesis: most named houses raised targets (Phillip, Citigroup, Goldman, Citic, Seaport), which typically reflects higher modeled data-center revenue, but two moves cut against it (Itau BBA lowered to $218.00, and Seaport raised its target while still assigning a sell rating).

confidence.basis: Inference from third-party price targets carried by one low-tier secondary aggregator; no vendor guidance figure is quoted and the targets disagree materially.

dispersion: Targets span $180.00 to $315.00 against a stated average of $324.23; Itau BBA cut from $256.00 to $218.00 while Citic raised from $242.00 to $315.00.
